# 1 Enoch Chapter 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 1 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 1:2 — 'parable' vs. 'discourse' for Ge'ez mesla

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "parable" | Traditional rendering; cognate with Hebrew mashal |
| LOGOS | "discourse" | More accurate for the genre — this is prophetic speech, not a parable in the NT sense |
| PNEUMA | "lifted up his voice" | Dynamic rendering of the idiom; focuses on the act of speaking |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'discourse' (LOGOS). The Ge'ez mesla here introduces prophetic revelation, not a comparison or riddle. 'Parable' (EMET) imports NT connotations. PNEUMA's 'lifted up his voice' captures the performative aspect but loses the technical term.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Terminological — the genre of the speech matters.

---

## 1:5 — 'Watchers' capitalization and identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Watchers shall-quake" | Preserves Ge'ez 'irin (cognate to Aramaic/Daniel 4:13) as proper noun |
| LOGOS | "the Watchers shall tremble" | Capitalized as a class of beings; 'tremble' more precise than 'quake' |
| PNEUMA | "The Watchers will shake" | Direct, visceral language |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three agree on capitalizing 'Watchers' as a proper class designation. Adopted 'tremble' (LOGOS) as more precise than 'quake' (EMET) or 'shake' (PNEUMA). The Watchers are the fallen angels of chapters 6-16.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. All three aligned on the key term.

---

## 1:9 — Jude 14-15 parallel — rendering of 'ten thousands of holy ones'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "with-ten-thousands of-His-holy-ones" | Preserves Ge'ez number + construct literally; cf. Jude 14 en muriasin |
| LOGOS | "with ten thousands of His holy ones" | Retains the specific number-idiom; preserves intertextual link to Jude |
| PNEUMA | "with countless thousands of his holy ones" | The Ge'ez/Greek number is idiomatic for 'an innumerable host' — translate the meaning |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'with ten thousands of His holy ones' (EMET/LOGOS). This verse is directly quoted in Jude 14-15, making the precise wording significant for intertextual study. The archaic 'ten thousands' (= myriads) preserves both the number and the echo.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Intertextual significance with Jude 14-15.

---
